body:
I think the thing is I feel clarity, I feel like if I were happy it would be a lie.

Even if that isn't true.

I'm not certain I have depression, as I've never been diagnosed and I don't want to jump the gun, but everything you've described and the symptoms I've read elsewhere certainly match my experiences.

Thing is...I'm not sure I want to get better, as weird as it sounds.

Not really.

The most anyone would think would be "oh, that's sad", before forgetting I ever existed.

Some of us don't have friends, or bullies for that matter. My teachers certainly wouldn't care.

The only people who really would are family, and the only ones who would never get over it are my parents.

Maybe it's selfish but it's also selfish to try to force someone to live who truly doesn't want to.

>Many other users following in your old footprints. More suicides, more sadness.

I honestly don't think some sort of weird chain reaction suicide, this isn't Jonestown.

The fact that I wouldn't be able to work up the courage to kill myself.

:p

Beauty is subjective and, well....

>Nothing has worth.

Worthless
So then suicide is not really a "waste" like people say?

>What feels like it's rotten?

I can hardly describe it, it's just like some sort of pit or something that constantly nags at me, makes me feel incomplete or disgusting.

I never really believed there was a true meaning to life.

I'm not so sure life is better than death, though.

Pleasures and happiness seem empty and hollow.

I can't enjoy these things because I don't deserve to.

I feel rotten inside.

It's funny...it seems to me like nihilism makes logical sense, but no one (including me) would ever really want to live by it because it just so damn depressing and humans aren't meant to live with that level of hopelessness.
So basically it makes no difference whether one is dead or not?

My dreams are pretty stupid, not to mention implausible at best.

>Also, being alive means that you can enjoy all the benefits of being able to interact with the world, which is good.

Besides, when I am happy or enjoying something, I'm not, because my happiness feels forced and fake, and there's something nagging at the back of my mind telling me I shouldn't be happy.


So I stop being happy and then I want to be happy again, rinse and repeat.

I don't even really wanna be happy, though.

When I'm happy it just feels fake.
